status: LOCAL IMPLEMENTATION PASS / NOT DEPLOYED / NO INDEPENDENT REVIEW
claim: A lost or silent volume reporter is no longer necessarily permanent. The policy authority may propose a replacement that takes effect after a 90-day public notice, and a policy may declare a silence floor at creation that engages after 180 to 730 days of silence. Nothing here was sent to any cluster.
supersedes: This retracts one statement, and only one: evidence/B2_LOCAL_VALIDATION_2026-08-19.json lists oracle_replacement under absent_by_construction, and that is no longer true. Every other statement in that file and in evidence/B2_ABSOLUTE_CEILING_2026-08-20.json stands as recorded.

program.name: purpose_vault
program.rebuild_determinism: two consecutive local builds after touching a source file produced the same digest; this is a same-host check only and does not establish a verified build
program.surface_guard: surface::the_program_exposes_exactly_eight_instructions fails if a ninth entry point appears or the order changes

changes.what: propose_oracle, restricted to the policy authority and rejecting the default pubkey; execute_oracle_rotation, permissionless once ORACLE_ROTATION_NOTICE_SECONDS (90 days) has elapsed.
changes.invariant: a rotation restores who may report, never what was reported: eligible_volume, updated_at and report_count are untouched, so a stale input stays stale across the change and the incoming oracle must speak before any release resumes
changes.no_cancel_instruction: a second proposal replaces the first and restarts its clock; proposing the sitting oracle is how a proposal is withdrawn, which is a weaker power than a cancel and needs no extra entry point
changes.permissionless_execution: the authorisation was the proposal and the public already had 90 days; requiring the authority again would add a way for an aged, announced rotation to be silently withheld

changes.what: PolicyWindow.silence_floor and PolicyWindow.silence_grace_seconds, set at open_policy. Zero floor with zero grace is the default and keeps the previous behaviour exactly. A declared floor requires a grace period between 180 and 730 days.
changes.why_the_band: the minimum exceeds the 90-day rotation notice, so replacing a lost oracle is always the faster path and the floor is only reached when the authority that would rotate it is gone too
changes.why_both_or_neither: a floor with no grace would engage the instant an input went stale, which is a fallback in everything but name; a grace with no floor describes nothing
changes.not_a_fallback: the floor is a fixed number chosen in advance, never the last reported volume, and it is bounded by hard_ceiling like any other window

changes.what: The sentinel for "this oracle has never spoken" moved from updated_at == 0 to report_count == 0.
changes.found_by: a new integration test that failed with StaleMarketInput where the silence floor was expected to engage
changes.why_it_matters: a timestamp cannot carry that meaning: zero is also a real instant, and a report made at it was indistinguishable from no report at all. The LiteSVM fixture's clock starts at zero, so every fixture that reported at setup was in exactly that state — the covenant treated a report that had happened as one that never had.
changes.live_severity: no cluster has a unix_timestamp of zero, so this was not reachable on any real network; it was reachable in the test environment, which is where it was found

covenant_version.b1_unaffected: B1 implements v0.1 and its statements are unchanged; v0.3 alters no cap, rate, cliff or notice period
covenant_version.rejection_vector_5_qualified: "any release with zero eligible volume" now reads "with a fresh report of zero". A declared silence floor is a stated exception applying only where there is no fresh report at all, and a policy without a floor refuses in both cases.

known_limits: not deployed to localnet, devnet, testnet or mainnet
no published IDL: the Anchor CLI cannot run on the build host because of a glibc mismatch, and a hand-assembled IDL was deliberately not shipped

the rotation authority is the policy authority, a single key in every fixture. Whoever holds it can name themselves and report an inflated figure; that is bounded by the per-vault caps, the cliff, the approved need and the notice period, and visible for 90 days first, but it is not prevented
no multisig exists; Squads compatibility with B2's Signer constraints has not been tested on any cluster and is not claimed
silence_floor is zero in every fixture but one, so B2's default remains a permanent lock on a lost oracle; no production floor or grace value has been chosen
a policy that declares no floor still seals permanently if the oracle and the policy authority are both lost
hard_ceiling still has no production value and cannot be added after policy creation
which venues count toward eligible volume, and which addresses are excluded, is decided off chain
